headline: BEARISH
headline_tag: A month of steep losses; a brief bounce did not hold

action.title: CUT / defend tightly with a stop-loss
action.detail: Keep acquisition running but defend it tightly: the headline is BEARISH, Bitcoin is down about 5% in a week and about 23% in a month, the Rally watch drop window that opened on 11 November is still open, and the long-term trend has now flattened. Put every acquisition campaign on a 30-day return stop-loss and pause the ones that miss it, trim spend aimed at active traders (they tend to leave before conditions improve), and move messaging toward stablecoins, safety and education. Keep a reserve rather than cutting to zero; step acquisition back up only once price closes back above the 200-week average ($68,210) and then the 200-day average ($72,142). This is a budget posture, not trading advice.

reasons: Down about 23% over 30 days and about 22% over 90 days.
Price is about 19% under its 50-day average, 34 days in a row.
Fear & Greed is 11 (extreme fear); about $487M left US Bitcoin funds in the latest day.
Price is about 10% under its 200-week average; long-term trend now reads flat.
watch: Monday's jump to above $64,000 on the Nvidia news faded within hours, and the long-term trend has now slipped to flat, so even good news is not holding. A close above $63,250 and then $68,210 (the 200-week average) would be the first sign the drop is easing; a close below $58,952 (the 30-day low) would deepen it.
analysis: Bottom line: the headline stays BEARISH and, as of today, the long-term trend has also slipped from 'still up' to 'flat', so this is a time for calm, safety and careful spending, not promotions. Short term, the picture is weak: Bitcoin, near $61,389, has closed under its 50-day average for 34 days in a row, sits about 19% below it and about 24% under its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 11 out of 100. Nvidia's CEO returning lifted tech stocks sharply on Monday and Bitcoin briefly jumped above $64,000, but it fell back below $61,000 the same evening (PANews). A normal week lately swings about $3,971, so a close above $63,250 (the top of a typical week's swing) would turn the week up, a close below $58,952 (the 30-day low) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy; safety and explainer messages fit better than offers.

The next month leans clearly down: price is about 23% lower than 30 days ago and about 22% lower than 90 days ago, and about $487 million left the US Bitcoin funds in the latest day of data. News is softening that a little, as the US Justice Department filed to recover more than $1 billion of the Binance hack money and Abraxas Capital moved about $1.18 billion of Bitcoin off exchanges in three days (PANews). Bitcoin would have to win back $75,686 (the 50-day average) before the month can firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb. US inflation data lands on 25 November and the Fed meets on 8 December; keep bigger campaign pushes until after a clear turn.

Long term, the picture has now turned flat: the 200-day average is still rising (about 4% over 90 days), but price is about 15% under it, about 10% under its 200-week average and about 51% below its all-time high. Slow structural steps add a little, as US regulator CFTC now lets derivatives platforms count Bitcoin, Ether and stablecoins toward their reserves and the European Central Bank widened the blockchain assets it accepts as collateral (PANews). The recovery is only back on track while Bitcoin closes above $72,142 (the 200-day average); $68,210 (the 200-week average) is the floor price has slipped under, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. More weeks under the 200-week average would turn this picture down and make keeping existing users the main use of budget.

items.why: PANews reports Korea's Upbit and Bithumb flagged Sky Protocol's SKY token and its USDS stablecoin as trading-warning assets and suspended deposits, citing risks around the issuer.
